Spiced Wine

Served at: St. Catherine's Day

Serves 6Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Spiced Wine is a warm, aromatic beverage traditionally enjoyed on St. Catherine's Day, celebrated on November 25th. This festive drink combines red wine with a blend of spices and citrus, making it perfect for chilly autumn evenings and gatherings honoring St. Catherine.

Ingredients

  • 1 bottle (750 ml) dry red wine
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 orange, sliced
  • 1 lemon, sliced
  • 4 whole cloves
  • 2 cinnamon sticks
  • 2 star anise
  • 1/2 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg

Method

  1. In a large saucepan, combine the red wine and sugar over low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
  2. Add the orange and lemon slices, cloves, cinnamon sticks, star anise, grated ginger, and nutmeg to the wine.
  3. Heat the mixture gently, making sure it does not boil, and let it simmer on low for 15-20 minutes to allow the flavors to infuse.
  4. Strain the spiced wine through a fine mesh sieve to remove the spices and citrus slices.
  5. Serve warm in heatproof glasses or mugs, garnished with a fresh orange slice if desired.

Tips

  • Use a fruity, medium-bodied red wine like Merlot or Zinfandel for best flavor.
  • Avoid boiling the wine to preserve the alcohol content and prevent bitterness.
  • For a non-alcoholic version, substitute red grape juice and follow the same spice infusion steps.
